analysis_question: Within comparable preselection baseline strata, is 2011 repeat selection associated with subsequent advancement above the preselection lifetime peak?

2.meaning: Advancement from baseline 2 means reaching post-T0 scope >=3.

3.meaning: Advancement from baseline 3 means reaching apex scope 4.

excluded_from_common_strata.baseline_1: No repeat-selected comparator; one single-selected case only.
excluded_from_common_strata.baseline_4: Three repeat-selected cases but no upward room on the locked 0-4 scale and no single-selected comparator.

interpretation: The very large unadjusted major/apex advantage of repeat-selected people is strongly confounded by their much higher preselection baseline status.
After comparing people from the same upward-capable baseline strata, both baseline=2 and baseline=3 point toward more advancement among repeat-selected people.
The stratum-specific estimates are imprecise and individually non-significant; the CMH common OR of 2.43 has p=0.107.
Therefore the data are compatible with a possible incremental repeat-selection signal, but they do not provide confirmatory evidence at this sample size.
This is more accurate than saying either that repeat selection has no incremental signal or that repeat selection independently predicts future rise.
guardrails: Repeat selection occurs roughly one year after initial selection, so early post-2010 performance may influence the repeat decision (reverse causation).
CMH adjusts only for the coarse locked baseline score strata, not editorial category, age, domain, visibility, institution, or other confounders.
The 0-4 scale has ceiling effects, especially for baseline=4.
Small strata make estimates unstable; p-values are exploratory.
